fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 is defeated by G13 affine closure: any linear discriminant or Construction-A map sending all honest encodings to one class also sends their coefficient-sum-one affine combination to that class. Code distance says nothing about this zero-class attack, and the proposed block replacement does not enlarge the encoding or otherwise break the collision.

Proposal 2 does not meet polynomial size: squarefree moments through degree d=O(log m) number n^{O(log m)}, generally quasipolynomial rather than polynomial. Low-degree Macaulay rows remain linear and admit pseudomoments until a refutation degree is reached; the three-variable all-eight-clauses instance has an elementary degree-three contradiction and cannot discriminate the required asymptotic degree.

Proposal 3 leaves the edge labels, representations, twisted target, fiber initialization, weights, and matched control unspecified. Twisted conservation is still linear, so affine combinations of paths with identical twisted boundary survive; testing two unfrozen representations only against the G19 shell cannot establish that completeness boundaries coincide or that a common signed kernel is absent.

Proposal 4 offers only constant-size local shell separation. Even a forbidden label beyond 2R gives only additive local cost against a completeness radius accumulated over many clauses, while G5 overlap, G13 affine combinations, and G15 threading remain untreated; the dimension-six search therefore cannot discriminate polynomial-gap scaling.

Proposal 5 either attaches fingerprints to exponentially many complete assignments or requires the unspecified multiplication-table lift already threatened by G19/G20 signed splicing. The 16-state experiment merely checks the direct Vandermonde property and omits the arithmetic circuit, Construction-A lift, unrestricted CVP objective, baseline, and control where the actual blocker occurs.

Proposal 6 cannot encode nonnegativity, bounded remainders, or rounding semantics using the stated unrestricted linear lattice rows; G1 negative slack and carry-table splicing remain live. A uniformly generated polynomial-size CG contradiction for every unsatisfiable formula is also an unsupported proof-complexity assumption, and two rounds on the easy three-variable obstruction do not test rank or size growth.

G7 verifies a zero-residual signed selector defeating all radix rows, and G19 verifies a zero-residual accepting signed flow with two negative coefficients. These directly undermine linear quotient, carry-table, and transition-conservation lifts.

G9 and G11 find constant-cost parity kernels under degree-two and degree-three moments, while G12 finds a cheaper clause-drop attack against a nonlinear-looking Walsh tag. These finite results provide no bounded-degree or fingerprint scaling law.

G14 is only a shell exclusion through baseline plus 32 on one pair-bag instance and explicitly supplies no composition theorem. None of the proposed local experiments addresses that missing growing-gap law.

No verifier evidence accompanies these six proposals, and the supplied status establishes no hardness lemma or dimension-dependent gap. Their proposed experiments are either underspecified or test an easy finite consequence rather than the stated causal blocker.
